name: beta_chg
rationale: Rising BTC beta = coin becoming a speculative/leveraged vehicle (attention, perp crowding); like lottery demand it is overpriced -> short.

name: beta_instab
params: w=0.10; std over 720h of 168h beta; high=short
rationale: Unstable BTC exposure = regime-shifting speculative names and larger hedge error; investors overpay for such optionality; also reduces hedge noise on the long side.

name: iskew
rationale: Idiosyncratic skewness / lottery preference (Boyer-Mitton-Vorkink): positively skewed coins are overpriced.

name: phi
rationale: Positive residual autocorrelation = trending/pumped names with slow-moving speculative flow that later reverses; negative phi = noise around fair value.

name: fund_chg
rationale: Funding rising vs its recent level = leverage building on the long side -> crowded, subsequent unwind.

name: fund_z30
rationale: Funding abnormally high vs own history = temporary long crowding (level is already in S0; this is the time-series surprise).

name: fund_vol
rationale: Volatile funding = unstable leverage/speculative demand; squeeze-prone and overpriced.

name: amihud
rationale: Illiquidity premium (Amihud 2002): within the liquid tercile, less liquid coins should earn more.

name: turn_trend
rationale: Rising turnover = attention shock / retail inflow -> overpricing that reverses (slower than failed 24h volume shock).

name: age
rationale: New listings underperform (unlock/vesting supply overhang, IPO-style overpricing, market-maker inventory unwinds).

name: volvol_div
rationale: Volatility rising without matching volume = thin, fragile market (liquidity withdrawal) -> worse future returns / crash risk.

name: hod_season
params: w=0.10; sum over the next held hours (i+2..i+9) of each coin's 30d same-hour mean residual; high=long
rationale: Heston-Korajczyk-Sadka intraday periodicity: recurring hour-of-day flows (funding times, regional sessions) repeat.

name: dow_season
params: w=0.10; same with 12-week same-weekday-hour mean residual; high=long
rationale: Day-of-week/weekend periodicity in coin-specific flows (weekend retail, thin books).

name: btc_delay
params: w=0.10; sum of 336h lag-1..3 BTC betas; high=long
rationale: Hou-Moskowitz price delay: slow-to-react (neglected) coins earn a premium; negative lag betas = overreaction/speculative names -> short.

name: coskew
rationale: Harvey-Siddique coskewness: coins that do well idiosyncratically when BTC makes big moves are hedges and are overpriced; negative coskew earns a premium.

name: rev3_h1
params: score=3h resid sum, every=1, N=NS=12, sf .5, stop .2; 25% risk weight vs B
rationale: Diagnostic showed alts overreact to BTC (lag-1..3 betas negative) and 1-6h residuals revert (IC ~0.018 at i+2): liquidity provision to hourly flow. Needs fast rebalance so tested as own sleeve.

name: age_sleeve
params: score=-age, every=8, N=NS=20, sf .5, stop .2; 25% risk weight
rationale: Stand-alone new-listing short / seasoned long book, low correlation with idio-vol book.

name: fund_chg_sleeve
params: pre-registered rule (best T-features at w=0.10 by t vs B get a 25% sleeve; age and fund_z30 already = S04/S05 so next in line): fund_chg, every=8, N=NS=20

name: dow_season_sleeve
params: next in line after fund_chg (t -1.0522 vs iskew -1.0525): dow_season, every=8, N=NS=20

name: near_high
params: w=0.10; log C - log max(C,720h), negated; near 30d high=long
rationale: George-Hwang 52-week-high anchoring: investors under-react near the high (continuation), coins far below their high keep being sold (capitulation/unlock overhang).

name: jump_beta
params: w=0.10; 720h beta on hours |rb|>2sd minus beta on other hours, negated; high jump beta=long
rationale: Bollerslev-Li-Todorov: exposure to BTC jumps (crash co-movement beyond normal beta) is priced; investors demand a premium to hold it. Distinct from total beta (BAB failed).

name: near_high_sleeve
params: near_high as own book every=8 N=NS=20; 25% risk weight

name: jump_beta_sleeve
params: jump_beta as own book every=8 N=NS=20; 25% risk weight

name: fund_disp_gross
params: B with hourly gross = clip(xs std of funding in M / its 90d rolling median, 0.5, 1.5)
rationale: When funding dispersion is high, leverage crowding in high-funding names (the short leg) is extreme and the funding/idio premium is larger; scale up then.

name: fund_disp_gross_inv
params: POST-HOC (after G01 gave t -4.3): gross = clip(90d median / disp, 0.5, 1.5); validated only via walk-forward over {B, G01, G02} and plateau
rationale: High funding dispersion marks alt-season / leverage manias when high-funding shorts get squeezed (the Mar-2021 max drawdown was such a squeeze); de-risk then. Rationale written after seeing G01, so treat as data-mined.

name: absmove6
params: w=0.10; |6h residual sum|; high=short. NOTE: motivated by diag_rev.py (full-sample bucket means), so partly data-snooped
rationale: Liquidation cascades / attention: coins with an extreme recent idiosyncratic move in EITHER direction underperform over the next hours (bottom 5% of 3h resid: -2.8 bp/h, top 5%: -1.5 bp/h at i+2). A fast complement to the 336h idio vol.

name: absmove6_h4
params: score=|6h resid|, every=4, N=NS=12, 25% risk weight

name: absmove24_h8
params: score=|24h resid|, every=8, N=NS=20, 25% risk weight
rationale: same as T35 at the book's own horizon

name: idio_2f
params: w=0.25; 336h std of residual after BTC and ETH (ETH-residual factor, 168h betas); high=short
rationale: Part of BTC-residual vol is common alt/ETH-factor exposure, which is systematic (squeeze/alt-season risk) rather than the lottery-type idiosyncratic vol the book is paid for; a purer idio measure should rank better.

name: idio_2f
rationale: same as T37 (near-replacement of the idio leg)
